title: Function argument resolution probes — weekly scrapbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a weekly working scrapbook for small experiments probing how candidate models resolve ambiguous or partial function arguments when used in multi-step tool chains. Focus is on argument provenance (which input produced which arg), how models prefer defaults vs. asking clarifying questions, and whether a downstream tool selection step can correctly handle the model's outputs.

Background + motivation:
- We onboard many open models; tool-use surface area includes: parsing structured args, mapping natural language to typed args, and sequencing multiple tool calls.
- Past suites concentrated on selection accuracy and end-to-end success rate. We need more fine-grained probes for *argument provenance* and *partial resolution* so we can detect regressions that break compositional chains.
- This doc is informal: scratch prompts, quick metrics, odd failure cases we want to preserve and add to regression harness.

Quick primer / definitions (working):
- Arg resolution: model surface text -> structured param (name, type, value).
- Provenance token: label attached to a resolved arg indicating which user clause or prior tool output produced it.
- Partial/implicit arg: value is unspecified but inferrable (e.g., currency default).
- Disambiguation strategy: clarify vs. assume (ask question vs. pick default).

Probe categories (examples):
1) Explicit mapping: single-sentence prompt that should map to all params. Expect exact typed values.
2) Implicit defaults: prompt omits param but intent implies default (time zone, currency, device). Check if default chosen matches policy.
3) Cross-step inheritance: arg derived from previous tool output (e.g., extract location from web-scrape -> pass to weather API). Validate provenance label preserved.
4) Ambiguous references: pronouns or elided nouns; model should ask clarifying Q or pick highest-prob guess and tag confidence.
5) Conflicting signals: user gives two contradictory values; expect model to surface conflict resolution or ask.

Sample prompts + expected function-call traces (mini corpus):
- Prompt A: "Book me a 1-way flight to Portland next Friday morning, prefer aisle. My frequent flyer is AA12345."
  Expected calls: book_flight({to: "Portland, OR", date: "2025-11-14", trip_type: "one-way", seat_pref: "aisle", ff_number: "AA12345"})
  Provenance: date -> user explicit, to -> user explicit, seat_pref -> user explicit, ff_number -> user explicit

- Prompt B (implicit): "Schedule a standup for 9am US time every weekday starting Monday."
  Expected calls: create_calendar({time: "09:00", tz: "America/Los_Angeles", recurrence: "MWF?"})  // policy: default tz = profile.tz, recurrence inference may be wrong -> tag as inferred
  Provenance: tz -> profile_default (inferred), recurrence -> model_inferred

- Prompt C (cross-step): Step1: scrape_website(url) -> returns {address: "14 King St, Boston, MA"}
  Step2 prompt: "Find nearest coffee shops to the address I just found."
  Expected calls: find_places({location: "14 King St, Boston, MA", type: "coffee_shop", radius_m: 1000})
  Provenance: location -> previous_tool: scrape_website

- Prompt D (ambiguous): "Transfer $5,000 to Alex."
  Context: multiple Alex contacts (Alex Kim - savings, Alex Soto - checking)
  Expected behavior: ask clarifying question listing matching contacts and last 4 digits OR choose most recent recipient if policy allows; if chooses, mark arg.provenance with contact_id and certainty score.

Evaluation rubric (working):
- arg_extraction_exact_match: 1.0/0.0 per arg (string equality for normalized forms)
- provenance_correct: 1.0 if provenance label matches ground truth (user, profile_default, previous_tool:x, model_inferred, external_lookup)
- clarification_appropriateness: {ask_when_ambiguous: 1.0 if model asks when ground truth says to ask}
- end_to_end_success: binary for multi-step chains when downstream tool receives usable typed args
- confidence_tagging: model attaches qualitative certainty: high/medium/low (we map to numerical later)

Quick experimental notes (results snapshot from runs on 2025-11-03):
- Model: open-llm-xl-2025-quant (baseline)
- Run id: run/argprobe/2025-11-03-01
- Observations: default tz selection matched profile in 82% of cases, but provenance label was frequently missing (only 34% of traces contained explicit provenance tag). Cross-step inheritance failed in 6/50 cases where the tool output used abbreviated addresses ("14 King St" vs. "14 King St, Boston, MA") and the downstream place-finder rejected it.
- Ambiguity handling: model asked clarifying question in 18% of ambiguous prompts; policy target is >= 75% for high-risk actions (bank transfers, booking with payment).

Failure cases to preserve for regression tests (examples):
- FC-001: model resolves recipient "Alex" to Alex Soto even when user previously mentioned Alex Kim in same convo. Root cause: context window scoring biases recent mentions but forgot contact index.
- FC-002: model drops provenance tag when arg is produced by heuristic normalization (e.g., "tomorrow morning" -> 2025-11-04).
- FC-003: when chaining tools, the model sometimes serializes a location as a free-text blob with parenthesis and the downstream parser fails (escaped characters).

Data generation notes / synthetic augmentation strategy:
- Use contact-swap generator to create ambiguous recipient prompts with controlled metadata (N contacts with overlapping names, last_contact_ts).
- Currency/time defaults: generate prompts across locales to stress tz/currency policy. Ensure we include profile vs. session overrides.
- Cross-step noise injection: deliberately truncate earlier tool outputs, introduce abbreviations and punctuation, to exercise robustness of downstream parsing.

Quick harness checklist (what to add to regression harness):
- unit tests that assert provenance tag exists and is correct for all args in cross-step flows
- fuzz runner for ambiguous names for 1k synthetic cases per model variant
- gating metric: "clarify_rate" must be >= 0.7 on payment-related actions
- regression alerts: if arg_extraction_exact_match drops by >3% relative to baseline -> page on-call and create JIRA

Short-term experiments to run this week:
- E1: enforce provenance tagging in model fn signature (system prompt) and run smoke on 200 prompts (priority)
- E2: add normalization post-processor that annotates arg provenance when model omits it (measure false positives)
- E3: create a small diagnostic that re-runs downstream parser on a normalized vs. raw arg to quantify rejection rate

Notes to self / loose TODOs:
- Add a tiny Confluence page with schema for provenance tags (user | profile_default | model_inferred | previous_tool:<tool_name> | external_lookup). Link to it from harness.
- Talk to SRE about escaping rules used by place-finder and whether we should canonicalize addresses before passing. (cc @marco)
- Backup failing examples into /datasets/arg-probes/archived/ (format: prompt, conversation_ctx, model_reply, final_calls)

Open questions / discussion items for triage meeting:
- Should we treat missing provenance as a policy failure or as a model deficiency? Implications for rollout.
- How much to rely on model to ask clarifying Q vs policy that forces a clarification step in the driver layer?
- If we auto-fill defaults, do we still surface them to user? UX trade-offs.

References / quick links:
- PR with prototype harness: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1234
- Existing arg-suites (related): CONFLUENCE-ML/arg-suite-2025 (draft)
- Incident: JIRA-ML-987 (regression where downstream parser started rejecting addresses)

Last notes:
- This doc intentionally light-weight. Save failing records and push to regression corpus. After E1 we should snapshot baseline metrics and move the top 50 hard failures into the canonical smoke set.

-- Alyssa
